coordinate_system.orientation_notes: Y follows the tube and bore axis, with +Y toward the open rim. Section views lie in XY with Z normal to the cut plane. Top views lie in XZ and look along -Y. Datum A locates the central axis but does not establish an axial origin plane or angular clocking.

relationships.detail: The finished exterior and main bore share the central tube axis.
The formed exterior and datum bore share the central tube axis.
The manufacturing hole is explicitly centered on the main part axis.
The dashed internal clearance envelope is centered within the main tube cavity.
The equally spaced bolt-circle holes are arranged around the datum bore axis.
The hole-pattern position control references datum A, defined by the main inner bore.
The central manufacturing hole and peripheral hole pattern open through the same bottom wall.
The central manufacturing hole passes through the formed bottom wall.
The bolt-circle holes pass through the formed bottom wall.
The enlarged rim transition joins the finished outside cylindrical surface.
The permitted outer-edge transition terminates at the annular end flat.
The annular end flat borders the opening of the main bore.
The formed outside bottom radius joins the unmachined cylindrical wall.
The formed outside bottom radius joins the bottom wall.
The finished opening-end flat and bottom base wall occupy opposite axial ends of the cup.
The formed top rim and closed bottom wall occupy opposite axial ends of the cup.
The explicitly unmachined exterior supplies the stock condition for the finished cylindrical exterior.
The explicitly unmachined bottom wall supplies the stock condition for the finished base wall.

datums.description: Inner bore cylinder of the unmachined tube.

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: Datum A establishes the bore axis and is the sole datum referenced by the hole-pattern position control. No secondary or tertiary datum is defined. Circularity of the finished exterior is a form control and does not introduce another datum.

assumptions.text: The machined top-view exterior is grouped with the machined section exterior using the section-cut reference and central-axis correspondence. The section observation is canonical because it carries the dimensional limits and circularity control.

The main bore observations are grouped on Signal 5: their feature types, diameter limits, blind-cavity condition, and tube-axis context agree. The unmachined section is canonical because it explicitly defines datum A and provides converted surface roughness.

The unmachined and finished exterior observations are retained as separate process-state nodes. Their different dimensional requirements are intentional stock-versus-finished requirements, not truncation errors; combining them would mix incompatible limits.
The unmachined and finished bottom-wall observations are retained as separate process-state nodes because their thickness requirements differ intentionally.

The VIEW Z marker attached to the main bore identifies the rim region rather than an identity between the bore and either detail feature. The end flat and outer-edge transition remain distinct singleton features.
The forming-stage top rim remains separate from the finished detail end flat: there is no direct identity reference or matching dimensional evidence connecting those observations.
The formed bottom radius remains a singleton requirement of the unmachined condition. It is not automatically imposed as the finished corner profile.
The section extraction notes establish that the bottom-wall openings are through-holes. The top-view geometry-needs entries requesting hole depth do not create a genuine missing-depth question.
The dashed minimum-clearance envelope is retained separately from the main bore because it expresses an internal clearance requirement rather than another observation of the same cylindrical surface.
The radius-or-chamfer alternative in VIEW Z is treated as an intentional manufacturing choice within the stated bounds; no exact angle or radius clarification is required.
The outside bottom corner profile retains the as-formed geometry without a secondary finish-radius machining operation, conforming to the final finished envelope dimensions.
The asterisk references the 108 MIN. diameter requirement, indicating that the 108 mm minimum clearance diameter envelope extends down to the inside bottom surface.
